Title: A disabled user's existing session keeps working
Re-test note: Old token refused straight after the account is disabled: 200 before, 401 immediately after and 6 s later.

Title: Forecast/schedule engine crashes with a native abort inside the CP-SAT solver, and stays down
Re-test note: Crash injection: the CP-SAT solver process was killed mid-build. The engine stayed up (0 restarts), the build fell back to HiGHS and finished DONE ("cpsat: failed (the solver process ended without an answer)", "highs: feasible"). Each solve now runs in its own process.
Steps: Seen twice: (1) during scripts/demo-seed.mjs (forecast → schedule); (2) during the gateway's own test run, seconds after 'cancel stops a running build inside the engine' passed, while the next multi-group solve ran
Expected: A failed solve fails that one request; the engine keeps serving
Actual: 'Fatal Python error: Aborted' in ortools cp_model.Solve (backend/engine/scheduling.py:465, solve_cpsat) with the new cancel watchdog thread (scheduling.py:459, solver.StopSearch from another thread) alive. The whole process dies: every forecast and schedule request then returns 503 until someone restarts it. Earlier dead engines also left 3 hung server.py processes (each with 4 workers) running. Not reproduced on demand: 3 rounds of start → cancel → solve passed
Evidence: engine-crash-1.log (native stack of all threads); gateway-suite.txt (12 tests failed with ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE after the crash); /health engine:false
Recommended fix: Run each CP-SAT solve in a child process (the ProcessPool already exists) so a native abort kills one job, not the server; re-check the uncommitted StopSearch-from-watchdog change (prefer a solution-callback stop or the solver's own time limit); run the engine under a supervisor that restarts it and kills the whole process tree; alert on /health engine:false.

Title: Engine crashes on large solves and takes every running build down with it
Re-test note: Each solve now runs in its own process. CP-SAT still died natively on parts of S01, S05, S06 and S10 (exit code 0xC0000409), but only that process ended: the engine server itself had 0 crashes, other builds carried on, and every build finished. The crashes themselves are now DEF-48.
Steps: Schedule groups of 3,000–6,000 people (one week, 90 s limit). Runs: 12 groups together; then one at a time; then one at a time without splitting.
Expected: A solve that runs out of time or memory fails alone; the engine keeps serving
Actual: 15 engine crashes in the scale run (engine-supervisor.log; 17 counting the 2 earlier in the day). All 12 builds started together failed. One at a time: every group that the gateway splits into parts (S02, S03, S05 and the split runs of S09, S11) crashed the engine; S10 survived one crash. Logs: 'Fatal Python error: Aborted' (14; 2 of them show SCIP 'Insufficient memory for allocation' followed by an OR-Tools 'Check failed' abort), and one 'Windows fatal exception: access violation' in backends.py respond() while building the reply. The parts of one group are solved side by side in one engine process, each CP-SAT model plus the HiGHS/SCIP backups in memory at once.
Evidence: scale/engine-run-*.log, engine-supervisor.log; S11 whole: DONE 157 s, no crash; S11 in parts: crash
Recommended fix: Solve each part/solve in its own child process with a memory cap so a native abort kills one solve, not the server; skip the MIP backups (HiGHS/SCIP) above a candidate size they cannot handle; run parts one after another when memory is short; supervise the engine and retry the job after a restart.

Title: Preparing a large schedule freezes the gateway for every user
Re-test note: Normal builds no longer freeze the API: with two 4,000–6,000-person builds preparing at once for 2 hours, health checks had a median of 546 ms. But 21 of 435 took over 10 s and 7 got no answer within 30 s, and the over-limit request in DEF-31 still froze everything.
Steps: Start schedule builds for groups of 5,000–6,000 people; call GET /health and the admin app meanwhile
Expected: The API stays responsive while schedules are built in the background
Actual: Gateway pinned at 100% of one CPU core (Node main thread, 430→604 MB); /health timed out at 15–30 s continuously for 40+ minutes; DB sessions sat 'idle in transaction' waiting for the gateway; S03 spent 16 minutes preparing. Opening Schedule Quality for a 6,000-person group did the same for 2+ minutes.
Evidence: health-samples.jsonl; scheduleRoutes.ts ~598–640: candidates are built on the main thread, rebuilt up to 8 times at coarser settings, yielding only every 25 people
Recommended fix: Build candidates in a worker thread or in the engine; compute the candidate count arithmetically and pick the thinning level once instead of rebuilding the list; cap per-request CPU for report screens and cache their results.

Title: An over-limit schedule request is not refused — it runs 8½ minutes and then drops

Actual: 510 s, then the connection failed; /health afterwards showed Redis down; the gateway answered nobody meanwhile
Recommended fix: Estimate people × days × starts × lengths before building and refuse at once.

Title: The 'two builds at a time' limit is not enforced
Re-test note: All 13 builds were queued together; never more than 2 ran at once. The queue has a new problem with long builds, see DEF-47.
Steps: Queue 12 schedule jobs while the gateway is busy

Evidence: schedule_jobs rows at 14:35; scheduleJobs.ts tick(): the running-count check and the claim are separated by an await, and tick() runs from both a timer and every enqueue

Title: Jobs fail at once while the engine restarts, and timeouts are reported as 'engine not reachable'
Re-test note: The gateway now retries: its log shows 'ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE; trying again (attempt 2 of 3)' and 'ENGINE_CRASHED; trying again'. One build (S13) still failed with a 2-minute engine timeout while the database was recovering from a crash; it built on the next try.
Steps: Queue jobs during the ~60 s an engine takes to start; or solve a group whose call exceeds the gateway's gRPC deadline
Expected: Wait/retry with back-off; a timeout says it timed out
Actual: 8 jobs failed within 5 s each; S09 (no crash) failed after 172 s with 'The forecasting engine is not reachable'
Recommended fix: Retry engine-unavailable failures with back-off for a few minutes; distinguish DEADLINE_EXCEEDED from UNAVAILABLE in the message.

Title: At 3,000+ people the optimiser adds nothing: schedules are the greedy starting roster
Re-test note: Groups are now split into parts of 667–800 people that CP-SAT improves: S02 (failed in run 1) reached 83.1%, S09 95.1%, S11 96.5%. Where CP-SAT crashes (DEF-48) the part is still the greedy starting roster: all of S05 and S06, 2 of 8 parts of S01.
Steps: Schedule any group with ≥ 210,000 candidate shifts (S01, S06, S08, S11, S12, S13) with a 90 s limit
Expected: CP-SAT improves on the starting roster; or the screen says the result is unoptimised
Actual: Every one: 'cpsat: feasible (starting roster only), highs: unknown, scip: unknown, greedy: feasible', gap 1 (100%). Valid schedules, often 95–98% covered, but contract hours, preferences and fairness are not optimised. Only S04/S07 (≤ 75,000 candidates) were optimised.
Recommended fix: Split earlier (smaller parts, solved safely — see DEF-29), give large groups a longer default limit, and show 'starting roster only' prominently on the schedule.

Title: Large builds take 20–75 minutes when two run at once, almost all of it before the solver starts
Re-test note: Found in this re-test.
Steps: Queue the 13 SCALE builds together (2 run at a time) on a gateway that has been up for a few hours; S01's 24,288-shift schedule from the first run is published
Expected: A few minutes per group (the solver itself needs 1.5–3 minutes)
Actual: S01 20 min, S02 41 min, S03 76 min, S05 44 min for the build itself; the solver's share was 90–190 s. The gateway sat at 100% of one core while the engine was idle. On a freshly restarted gateway, one build at a time, groups of 3,000–4,000 took 4–9 minutes.
Evidence: Job progress stayed on 'Preparing' for 17–40 min; process CPU sampling; solver wallSec in each schedule's statistics
Recommended fix: Profile candidate preparation. Every candidate shift scans tenant-wide arrays: all approved time off, all 2,008 availability rows and every published shift of other groups (blockedReason, preferenceFor). Index them by employee once (Map) before the loop, and move preparation off the API process (worker thread or the engine).

Title: The queue fails or repeats builds that are still running
Re-test note: Found in this re-test.
Steps: Run two large background builds at once, or one long build, and watch schedule_jobs
Expected: A running build keeps its slot and its status until it finishes
Actual: While a build prepares, its heartbeat falls more than 30 s behind, so the sweeper hands it back to the queue while it is still running. S02 and S05 were built twice (two S02 versions). S05 showed QUEUED while running. S09 and S10 failed with 'The server restarted twice while this was running' with no restart, and S10 saved an empty version. After the laptop's standby, S05's finished build was overwritten as FAILED.
Evidence: wfm.schedule_jobs attempts = 2–3 with a fresh heartbeat on a QUEUED row; two 'SCALE S02 rerun' versions; gateway log
Recommended fix: Send the heartbeat from outside the busy event loop (or make preparation yield properly), give the sweeper a much longer grace period, never overwrite a DONE job, and make a job's run single-owner (check the worker and attempt before writing results).

Title: CP-SAT crashes on many parts, so those parts get only the starting roster
Re-test note: Found in this re-test.
Steps: Build S05 (5,000 people, two skills) or S06 (4,000 people, leave and availability) as a background plan
Actual: The solver process ended with exit code 0xC0000409 (a native abort) on every part of S05 and S06 and on 2 of 8 parts of S01. HiGHS and SCIP returned 'unknown', so those parts used the greedy roster. In S05, 1,000 people got no shifts at all.
Evidence: Schedule statistics: 'part 1: cpsat: failed (the solver process ended without an answer (exit code 3221226505))'
Recommended fix: Capture the worker's stderr and a core dump to find the abort (often memory, or a model OR-Tools rejects); try fewer search workers or a per-process memory limit; report 'starting roster only' on the schedule when every solver fails.

Title: The gateway stopped again with no log line, right after an engine crash
Re-test note: Found in this re-test.
Steps: Background build of S10 (13-week plan); the engine's solver crashed and the gateway logged 'ENGINE_CRASHED; trying again'
Expected: The gateway retries the build, or logs why it stops
Actual: The gateway process ended with exit code 127 and nothing more in its log. This is the second time (release-gate DEF-44). The build failed and was retried after the gateway was back.
Evidence: Gateway log ends on the ENGINE_CRASHED line followed by 'gateway exit=127'
Recommended fix: Log uncaughtException, unhandledRejection and process exit before quitting; run the gateway under a supervisor that restarts it.

Title: Screens that load every employee became very slow once the 2,000 limit was lifted
Re-test note: Found in this re-test.
Steps: Open Workforce > Time off in Chrome on the 50,656-person organisation; call GET /workforce/employees with no paging
Expected: A few seconds, as in the first run (3.1 s)
Actual: Time off took 72 s to settle (first run 3.1 s). The unpaged employee list takes 40 s and sends 42 MB with nothing else running. The Employees screen itself pages and opens in 3.9 s.
Evidence: probe-ui and probe-api rows in the run-2 results
Recommended fix: Make every screen and picker that needs employees use paging or a search endpoint (names and ids only), and cap or refuse the unpaged list on large organisations.
